findings.title: previewSplit reports no public-trigger coverage after sub-1-USDG growth while a public split succeeds (stale pre-A1 coverage rule)
findings.evidence: Found while triaging the slither incorrect-equality and timestamp results on previewSplit (SleeveTrade.sol:187-193). SleeveTrade.sol:184 sets `preview.publicReadyAt = observedAt + env.grace` only when `observedAt != 0 && preview.unsorted <= acct.observedUnsorted`, the rule from before the audit A1 dust fix. observe (SleeveTrade.sol:78) and the public split (`_requireSplitGrace`, SleeveTrade.sol:516) both treat `unsorted < uint256(acct.observedUnsorted) + OBSERVE_RESTART_GROWTH` (1e6) as covered. So one base unit sent after an observation makes previewSplit return publicReadyAt 0 ('no observation covers the unsorted amount yet') until a sort clears the observation or 1 USDG more arrives, while observe called for the dust changes nothing and a PUBLIC split after the grace succeeds. A public trigger or app that waits for a non-zero publicReadyAt never fires the fallback, which reopens the R1 MEDIUM dust griefing for preview-driven callers at one base unit per observation. The keeper's own KEEPER trigger is unaffected and the onchain rule is correct. PoC (passes): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-v/contracts/test/audit/StaticTriagePreviewGrace.t.sol, test_previewSplit_reportsNoCoverage_whileAPublicSplitSucceeds: pay 500 USDG, stranger observes (preview = observedAt + 3600), pay 1 base unit, observe returns the same observedAt, warp to observedAt + 3600, previewSplit.publicReadyAt == 0, then the stranger's split writes a PUBLIC FILLED receipt with usdgIn 500000001. Run: `FOUNDRY_OUT=out-static FOUNDRY_CACHE_PATH=cache-static forge test --match-path test/audit/StaticTriagePreviewGrace.t.sol` gives 1 passed. The A1 fix also left the docs on the old rule: SPEC.md:94-95, D-009 Q15, and the ISleeveModule NatSpec of Observed (ISleeveModule.sol:354, 'A public split may sort at most this much') and observe (ISleeveModule.sol:621-623, 'grew past the stored amount'). No DECISIONS entry records the 1 USDG threshold.
findings.fix: Add one private predicate in SleeveTrade, `_covers(acct, unsorted)` returning `acct.observedAt != 0 && unsorted < uint256(acct.observedUnsorted) + OBSERVE_RESTART_GROWTH`, and use it in observe, `_requireSplitGrace` and previewSplit (`if (_covers(acct, preview.unsorted)) preview.publicReadyAt = acct.observedAt + env.grace;`). Keep the PoC as the regression test. Bring SPEC section 8, D-009 Q15 and the ISleeveModule NatSpec of Observed, observe and SplitPreview.publicReadyAt in line, and add a DECISIONS entry for the 1 USDG restart threshold.

findings.title: One base unit donated to the module blocked every buy (absolute-balance I1 check)
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 0 to 4 (0-based in audit_r1_raw.json), five lenses with the same root cause. Lines are at 6535108 (audit-v), e16bb96 lines in parentheses. At e16bb96, SleeveBuy.execute called _requireNothingHeld(usdg) and _requireNothingHeld(token) after the swap (lines 39-40, 115-118), reverting ModuleHoldsFunds whenever balanceOf(module) != 0. That checked the module's absolute balance, not what the call changed. Anyone can transfer USDG or a stock token to the module (USDG has no recipient restriction and Stock.transfer only checks the blocklist), the module is immutable (D-019) with no sweep, and SleeveTrade._buy rethrows every revert except PremiumAboveCap, so the whole split or settle reverted for every account. Triage in AUDIT_R1.md: FIXED in 9a6edba. At 6535108 execute snapshots both module balances before _swap (lines 38-40) and _requireNothingKept (lines 119-122) reverts when either changed. Regression test: contracts/test/unit/SleeveModuleSplit.t.sol:378 test_I1_split_donationToModule_doesNotBlockBuys (split only, no settle case). Verifier: reproduce on e16bb96, confirm the PoCs no longer reproduce on 6535108, and check what the fix left. PRD I1 (PRD line 355, 'holds no USDG and no stock tokens before or after any call'), docs/SPEC.md lines 14, 131 and 186 and the execute NatSpec (SleeveBuy.sol line 25) still state the absolute form, as does claim 3.7 in docs/CLAIM_LEDGER.md ('The module holds none of them after any call'), and no DECISIONS entry records the change. The build contract treats a change to how a PRD invariant holds as an owner decision. ModuleHoldsFunds reports the absolute balance, not the delta. The component 6 sell must use the same delta.
findings.scenario: Attacker calls USDG.transfer(sleeveModule, 1). From then on every split whose guard reaches the buy reverts ModuleHoldsFunds(USDG, 1) for every account, and every settle reverts too. Sending 1 wei of SPY to the module does the same for every SPY buy. Splits only succeed when the guard queues, so equity piles up in buckets that can never settle. Recovery needs a new module and every account reinstalling. Funds are not lost: USDG stays spendable and buckets can be released. PoCs against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/funds_Donation.t.sol (test_oneWeiUsdgDonationBricksEverySplitBuy, test_oneWeiTokenDonationBricksSettle) and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/reentrancy_DustAndForgedRevert.t.sol (test_dustDonationBricksEveryBuy, test_tokenDustDonationBricksTickerBuys).
findings.fix: Measure I1 as a delta: read usdg.balanceOf(module) and token.balanceOf(module) before executeFromExecutor and revert ModuleHoldsFunds(asset, after - before) unless both are unchanged afterwards, which is the shape 9a6edba adopted. Use the same delta in the component 6 sell. Get the owner's agreement to restate PRD I1 as 'no call leaves the module holding more than before', then update SPEC sections 1, 11 and 17, the execute NatSpec and DECISIONS, and make the invariant suite assert the delta form. Optional: a permissionless sweep of stray module balances to a fixed sink would let the absolute form hold again.

findings.title: The caller-chosen quote makes the owner's slippage cap meaningless for keeper and public triggers, so every buy can be pushed to the premium cap
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 10 (oracle, MEDIUM), 25 (funds, LOW) and 38 (modern, LOW). AUDIT_R1.md lists entries 25 and 38 again under LOW, and also names the arithmetic lens here. The arithmetic report on this line (entry 50) is a different defect, kept as A1-37. minOut = amount * quote / 1e6 * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000 (lines 422-424, e16bb96 line 417), and quote comes from the trigger. _enter (line 499) only rejects zero, so quote = 1 gives a minOut of a few base units of an 18-decimal token. For KEEPER and PUBLIC triggers the only price bound is exceedsPremium against the Chainlink answer. That answer can trail the live price by up to the feed's 0.5 percent deviation trigger, and the check treats USDG as exactly 1 USD (A1-11). FCFS ordering stops outside sandwiches, but a self-sandwich fits in one transaction. PRD 7.4 (PRD line 181) defines slippage 'against the trigger's quote' and D-009 Q21 accepts the premium cap as the public caller's bound, but the app shows the rule's slippageBps (default 50) as a guard (app/src/components/sleeve/rule-summary.tsx:91, 'Slippage cap ... from the quote'). A stolen KEEPER key gets the same power with no grace on every default-keeper account (A1-22), which strains PRD 14's 'no authority beyond public functions'. Triage: ACCEPTED per PRD 7.4 and 14, with 'the app and SECURITY.md say so'. SECURITY.md does not exist and the app copy does not say slippage is void for non-owner triggers, so the verifier should check the acceptance against what is actually written.
findings.scenario: Rule: 100 bps premium cap, 50 bps slippage. The keeper is down for an hour, so the public grace elapses. An attacker contract buys SPY in an allowlisted pool to about 99 bps above the feed, calls split(account, pool, 1), then sells back. The receipt is FILLED with minOut 49 base units and premiumBps between 51 and 100. The PRD 7.4 worst case of about 1.5 percent at the default cap becomes the expected case for any non-owner trigger, and at the 500 bps maximum the attacker takes about 5.2 to 6 percent of each equity part minus pool fees. A compromised default keeper can do this to every account with no grace by ordering its own transactions or delegating with EIP-7702. C2 premiums will cluster at the cap. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/modern_PublicQuote.t.sol::test_publicQuoteOfOneVoidsSlippageAndFillsAtCap.
findings.fix: For KEEPER and PUBLIC triggers, floor minOut on chain at the feed-implied output: feedOut = amount * 10^(tokenDecimals + feedDecimals - usdgDecimals) / answer and minOut = max(callerMinOut, feedOut * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000), or reject a quote below the feed-implied quote by more than slippageBps. That makes slippageBps a real bound against the feed and closes the atomic sandwich beyond it. If the premium cap must stay the bound, fix the PRD 7.4 and app copy that present slippage as protection, create SECURITY.md with the residual, and record it in the claim ledger.

findings.title: The minimum-out check (PRD 7.4 step 9) runs before the premium check (step 8), so a fill above the cap reverts where the spec says it queues
findings.description: Raw entry 17 (e16bb96 line 105). PRD 7.4 orders step 8 (premium cap: queue the equity) before step 9 (trigger's minimum: revert). The router gets amountOutMinimum = minOut (_calls, line 108), and _swap checks TooFewTokens (line 78) before execute measures the premium (lines 45-56). When both fail, the call reverts with the router's 'Too little received' instead of queueing PREMIUM. That differs from PRD 7.4 and SPEC 9 step 9, and DECISIONS does not record it: D-009 Q12 describes the minimum-out revert but not its order against the premium.
findings.scenario: With the pool priced 150 bps above the feed, the keeper's quote queues PREMIUM, but the same split with quote * 2 reverts 'Too little received'. A pool pushed between the quote and inclusion reverts instead of queueing, so the keeper has to retry rather than getting a PREMIUM receipt. Safe, since nothing moves. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol::test_minOutIsCheckedBeforeThePremium.
findings.fix: Pass amountOutMinimum 0 to the router (sqrtPriceLimitX96 stays 0) and check minOut in SleeveBuy after exceedsPremium, reverting TooFewTokens there. Or record the reordering in DECISIONS and SPEC 9. If A1-06 adds a feed-implied minOut floor, apply the same ordering to it.

findings.title: Code inside the account batch can forge PremiumAboveCap and make split write a fake PREMIUM queue receipt
findings.description: Raw entry 26 (e16bb96 line 434). _buy (lines 439-453) catches any executeBuy revert that is 36 bytes long and starts with the PremiumAboveCap selector, treats it as the module's own premium check, and copies the encoded int256 into receipt.premiumBps. executeFromExecutor (SleeveBuy.sol line 71) bubbles raw revert data from everything that runs inside the batch: the account implementation, a Kernel executor hook the owner set on Sleeve's executor config (preCheck and postCheck run inside executeFromExecutor), the USDG facets, the stock token's beacon implementation, the router and the pool. Any of them can revert PremiumAboveCap(x) for any x. The receipt log then carries premium numbers and PREMIUM reasons the guard never produced, which the verifier cannot tell apart, and any batch revert becomes a soft queue where D-009 Q12 says the whole call reverts. Only the owner, against its own account, or the issuer can trigger it, so there is no third-party fund loss.
findings.scenario: The owner installs Sleeve with an executor hook whose postCheck reverts PremiumAboveCap(-4242), or the account is a custom ERC-7579 implementation, or a stock token implementation is upgraded to do it. The keeper's split catches the revert, queues the equity with reason PREMIUM, and writes a QUEUED receipt with premiumBps = -4242. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/reentrancy_DustAndForgedRevert.t.sol::test_forgedPremiumAboveCapIsCaughtAsPremiumQueue.
findings.fix: In SleeveBuy._swap, wrap executeFromExecutor in try/catch. If the inner revert data starts with the PremiumAboveCap selector, re-revert with a different error such as BatchReverted(bytes). Otherwise bubble it unchanged, so the router's minimum-out error still surfaces. Then the only PremiumAboveCap that can leave executeBuy is the one SleeveBuy.execute raises itself (line 56).

findings.title: A trigger-supplied quote can make the minOut mulDiv panic instead of reverting with a named error
findings.description: Raw entry 50 (e16bb96 line 417). minOut = Math.mulDiv(Math.mulDiv(amount, quote, 1e6), 10,000 - slippageBps, 10,000) (lines 422-424). quote is an unbounded uint256 from the keeper or a public caller, and _enter (line 499) only rejects zero. When amount * quote / 1e6 does not fit in a uint256, OpenZeppelin's mulDiv panics with 0x11. The build contract says every failed check reverts with a named custom error, and LedgerMath states that no input makes a function panic. Only the caller's own transaction fails and no state changes. Same expression as A1-06 but a separate defect: A1-06's minOut floor does not stop this overflow.
findings.scenario: The keeper calls split(account, pool, type(uint256).max) on a 500 USDG payment, and the call reverts Panic(0x11) from the minOut computation. The keeper and verifier get an unlabeled panic in place of a decodable error. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/arithmetic_Premium.t.sol::ArithmeticQuotePanicTest.test_hugeQuotePanics.
findings.fix: Bound the quote up front, for example revert QuoteTooLarge(quote) when quote > type(uint256).max / amount * 1e6. That bound can't overflow itself, because _buy only runs with amount >= minClip >= MIN_CLIP_FLOOR (1e6, SleeveModule.sol line 48). Or compute the product with Math.mul512 and revert a named error when the high word is at least 1e6.

findings.title: Dust transfers plus observe() kept the public trigger from ever firing for split and settle
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 8 (spec), 9 (dos) and 11 (access), all MEDIUM, and 28 (funds, LOW). AUDIT_R1.md lists entry 28 again under LOW, and its summary says the seven MEDIUM reports reduce to six issues. They reduce to five, because entries 8, 9 and 11 are this one finding. At e16bb96, observe() restarted observedAt whenever unsorted grew past observedUnsorted (line 73). A public split needed unsorted <= observedUnsorted and the grace since observedAt (_requireSplitGrace, line 509), and a public settle's readyAt took max(since, openedAt, observedAt) (_settleReadyAt, line 518). So one base unit of growth plus a permissionless observe() restarted both clocks. Separately, every split or settle that writes a receipt clears the observation for the whole account (_clearObservation, now line 535), so any split restarts the public settle clock of unrelated buckets. D-009 Q15 stops pre-aging, not pushing back. Triage: FIXED in 40682ef. OBSERVE_RESTART_GROWTH = 1e6 (line 65), and observe (line 78) and _requireSplitGrace (line 516) restart only on growth of 1 USDG or more. Regression test: contracts/test/unit/SleeveModuleSplit.t.sol:528 test_split_dustCannotPostponeThePublicFallback. Verifier, check what the fix left. (a) A griefer can still restart both clocks for 1 USDG per restart, which goes to the owner. Decide whether that bound is acceptable. (b) The settle half is unchanged: observedAt is still in _settleReadyAt (line 528), _clearObservation still runs after every split (line 110) and settle (line 301), and there is no settle regression test, so a keeper dust split, or a public dust split at the moment the split grace ends, clears the clock a pending bucket's public settle depends on. (c) previewSplit (line 184) still tests unsorted <= observedUnsorted, so its publicReadyAt disagrees with _requireSplitGrace for growth under 1 USDG. (d) A public split now also sorts up to 1 USDG minus 1 base unit that arrived after the observation without its own grace, while D-009 Q15 still says the clock restarts on any growth, and no DECISIONS entry records the threshold.
findings.scenario: The keeper is offline. A 500 USDG payment is observed at t0. Every 50 minutes a griefer sends 1 base unit of USDG to the account and calls observe(). At t0 + 9 to 10 hours a public split still reverts GracePeriodActive(now + 3600), and a queued bucket observed the same way stays refused to a public settle. The cost is about 1e-6 USDG plus gas per hour. A compromised keeper can do the same to public settles with dust plus keeper splits. Owner triggers still work, so funds aren't locked, but the PRD 7.2 and PRD 9 fallback (keeper down: anyone can trigger after the grace) is gone. PoCs against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol (test_dustEvery50MinutesBlocksPublicSplitIndefinitely, test_dustPlusObserveBlocksPublicSettleIndefinitely), /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/access_Observe.t.sol::test_access_dustObserveBlocksPublicSplitForever (24 rounds for 24 base units) and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/funds_Liveness.t.sol::test_dustGriefsPublicSplit. Rerun them on 6535108 with 1 USDG steps, and with keeper or public dust splits against a pending bucket, to measure the residual.
findings.fix: Don't let growth void an elapsed clock. For split: once observedAt + grace has passed, let a PUBLIC split sort only min(unsorted, observedUnsorted) and leave later arrivals on their own clock, or keep two observation slots (matured and pending) so growth never resets the amount already covered. Then _clearObservation clears only what the action consumed. For settle: drop observedAt from public settle readiness, since max(bucket.since, sessionOpenedAt) + grace already anchors it and dust cannot move bucket.since, or use a clock that is set only when pending is zero and that observe() and splits don't reset. 40682ef took the 'restart only when growth reaches a floor' option from entry 11. If it stays, align previewSplit, update D-009 Q15 in DECISIONS, and add a settle regression test next to test_split_dustTransferCannotPreAgeTheObservation.

findings.title: An equity part below the clip strands in its bucket once a later payment fills directly
findings.description: Raw entry 21 (e16bb96 line 247). A split whose equity part is under minClip queues it in the ticker's bucket with reason CLIP (line 252). A later split whose equity part clears the clip buys only its own part through _buy and leaves the bucket alone, and settle reverts BelowClip for any bucket under minClip (line 278). The bucket only grows if another sub-clip part arrives. The equity share is never invested and counts as pending, not spend, until the owner notices and releases it. Nothing is lost. Related: A1-31, where the same BelowClip check blocks a removed ticker's refusal.
findings.scenario: Default rule: 10 percent to SPY, 25 USDG clip. A 100 USDG payment queues 10 USDG with CLIP. A 1,000 USDG payment then fills 100 USDG directly. The 10 USDG bucket can't be settled by the keeper or the public. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/funds_Liveness.t.sol::test_subClipBucketStrandsAfterALaterFill.
findings.fix: In _sort, when the guard clears and the rule ticker's bucket is non-empty, add the bucket to the buy amount and settle it with the split, keeping I2 on the receipt and recording the bucket's since. Or let settle run on a bucket below the clip when the current split's equity part would cover it.

findings.title: The observation clock survives an owner outflow, so a later payment is publicly splittable with no grace
findings.description: Raw entry 33. observedAt and observedUnsorted are a cached snapshot of unsorted, cleared only by a split or settle that writes a receipt (SleeveTrade._clearObservation, called at lines 110 and 301). _bookOwnerOutflow (lines 428-446), which can drain unsorted at endOwnerOp, never clears or clamps them. Neither does split's reconcile branch (SleeveTrade.sol lines 102-106, which returns before _clearObservation) or release. After the owner spends the observed income, the stale observedUnsorted still covers later income up to that size, and observedAt is already past the grace. That breaks D-009 Q15 ('a payment cannot be pre-aged') and takes away the keeper's one-hour priority window for the new payment. The public caller then picks the pool and quote, bounded only by the premium cap (A1-06). Since 40682ef (A1-05) coverage is unsorted < observedUnsorted + 1e6 (SleeveTrade.sol line 516), which widens it by up to 1 USDG.
findings.scenario: A 500 USDG payment lands and a stranger calls observe, recording (T0, 500). Before any split, the owner withdraws 600 USDG in a bracketed batch, 100 from spend and 500 from unsorted, so unsorted is 0 and the observation is still (T0, 500). Five hours later a new 400 USDG payment arrives and a stranger calls split in the same block. _requireSplitGrace sees it covered and readyAt = T0 + 3600 in the past, so the PUBLIC split succeeds at once. PoC against e16bb96 (SleeveModule unchanged): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/transient_Audit.t.sol::test_staleObservationAfterOwnerOutflowSkipsGrace.
findings.fix: After an owner outflow in _bookOwnerOutflow, clear the observation or clamp observedUnsorted to the new unsorted. Do the same in split's reconcile branch and in release and _releaseBuckets when unsorted and the buckets are empty. Add a unit test: observe, bracketed withdraw, new payment, public split reverts GracePeriodActive.

findings.title: Any unsorted amount, down to 1 base unit, makes the keeper pay for a full split and receipt
findings.description: Raw entry 41 (e16bb96 line 97). split proceeds for any unsorted > 0. At default rules a 1 base unit payment gives equityPart 0, which still writes a QUEUED/CLIP receipt (A1-14), and a sub-clip equity part runs the whole guard (about 304k gas measured for QUEUED/CLIP). An attacker spending about 50k gas per dust transfer across many installed accounts makes a keeper that splits everything spend several times as much. Public triggers pay their own gas, so only the keeper is exposed.
findings.scenario: An attacker sends 1 base unit of USDG to 1,000 installed accounts. A keeper that splits any unsorted balance writes 1,000 receipts, draining its gas funding and adding noise to the receipt log.
findings.fix: Keeper policy: skip a split while unsorted is below a threshold, for example rule.minClip * 10,000 / equityBps, unless the oldest unsorted inflow is older than a set age. The contract could optionally refuse a non-owner split below a floor, but the off-chain threshold is enough. Record it as a keeper (component 7) requirement.

findings.title: A removed ticker's bucket below the current clip can't be refused to spend by settle
findings.description: Raw entry 42 (e16bb96 line 273). _settle checks BelowClip (line 278) before the guard, so the D-009 Q24 path (a removed ticker sends its bucket to spend as REFUSED_TICKER) applies only to buckets at or above the current rule's minClip. Smaller buckets wait until the owner calls release. A small deviation from Q24, and funds stay safe.
findings.scenario: An AAPL bucket of 10 USDG under a 25 USDG clip. The timelock removes AAPL. The keeper's settle reverts BelowClip, and the bucket stays pending until the owner releases it.
findings.fix: Run the step 1 and step 2 refusal checks (ticker inactive or without a feed, account blocked) before BelowClip in _settle, or note the exception in D-009 Q24.

groups.name: Price guard, feeds and USDG (PriceGuard, premium math, SleeveTrade._guard)

findings.title: An unscheduled closure or market-wide halt lets the held price pass the guard as live for the whole day
findings.description: Raw entry 5. readStockFeed (lines 226-241) rejects a round only when it is more than stockFeedMaxAge (25 hours) old or older than sessionOpenedAt. The calendar only knows a closure the timelock executed before 00:00 UTC on the day (SessionCalendarExtension.addClosure, line 183, D-017). A full-day closure lasts under 25 hours and the last round still postdates the session's opening, so for the whole unlisted closed day the guard returns NONE on a frozen price. Trading halts behave the same, including a level-3 circuit breaker that ends the day and a single-stock news halt. oraclePaused could flag them, but chain-constants shows it has never been used. SessionCalendarExtension.sol:181 ('a closure announced later is guarded only by PriceGuard') and D-017 ('guarded by PriceGuard's age, freshness, oraclePaused and premium checks') claim coverage the code does not give. Triage in AUDIT_R1.md: ACCEPTED and 'recorded in SECURITY.md', but no SECURITY.md exists in the repo at 6535108 or at HEAD 68cad5b, so the recorded acceptance is missing and both statements above are still wrong. PRD 14 answers 'Weekend or holiday gap' with 'Session calendar. Equity share queues.', and no PRD row accepts this gap. Related: A1-27 is the overnight form of the same symptom with a different root cause.
findings.scenario: A Hurricane Sandy style event or a short-notice national day of mourning closes NYSE and the 24 Hour Market on a Wednesday, and the timelock misses the addClosure deadline. The NVDA feed stops at Tue 19:59 EDT while the calendar still says Wednesday is open. A payment lands and the keeper splits, or a public caller after the grace, on a pool trading on news while the feed is frozen. The fill passes at up to premiumCap above the held price, and Thursday reopens 10 percent lower. Each unscheduled closure or halt exposes up to about 25 hours of payments. PoC against e16bb96 (PriceGuard unchanged since): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/oracle_HeldPrice.t.sol::test_unscheduledClosure_heldRoundPassesForTheWholeDay accepts a 24-hour-old round from before an unlisted closure with Reason.NONE.
findings.fix: Add a liveness test that does not depend on the calendar. One option: during a session, require the newest updatedAt across all active tickers' feeds to be within a market-liveness bound of 13 to 16 hours. In the audit week of rounds (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/notes/oracle_week_rounds.txt) the longest in-session gap across the four feeds was about 12 hours, Thu 15:50 to Fri 04:01 EDT. Another option: a same-day closure path that skips the 48-hour delay but can only close, never open. At minimum, correct the comment at SessionCalendarExtension.sol:181 and D-017, create SECURITY.md and record the gap there and in DECISIONS next to the missing sequencer feed (PRD 9).

findings.title: No post-change multiplier check, so the immediate updateMultiplier form never queues and a pre-change feed round is accepted right after effectiveAt
findings.description: Raw entry 14. checkMultiplier (lines 207-213) returns NONE whenever effectiveAt <= block.timestamp. The issuer's updateMultiplier(uint256) sets effectiveAt = block.timestamp (chain-constants section 3), so an immediate change never hits PRD 7.4 step 5 although it takes effect inside the guard window. For a scheduled change the guard queues only until effectiveAt and then accepts a round whose updatedAt is before effectiveAt. Dividend steps are under 0.5 percent, so the feed is not forced to post a new round. Research Q1 raised this and D-014 chose no after-clause, so part of it is a recorded decision. The open part is that nothing bounds the error if the feed's round and the switched multiplier disagree, and oraclePaused, the other corporate-action guard in PRD 14, has never been used.
findings.scenario: The issuer applies a 1:2 reverse split with the immediate form. If the feed's next round lags or is computed from mismatched parts, the guard clears, because effectiveAt == now gives NONE and the round is fresh by age, and a fill priced against a wrong answer passes the cap. Exposure depends on how the feed is built. PoC against e16bb96 (PriceGuard unchanged): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/oracle_Multiplier.t.sol (test_immediateMultiplierChange_neverQueues_andPreChangeRoundPasses, test_scheduledChange_oneSecondAfterEffectiveAt_preChangeRoundPasses).
findings.fix: In checkBuy, after readStockFeed, return MULTIPLIER (or STALE) when effectiveAt != 0 && effectiveAt <= block.timestamp && updatedAt < effectiveAt. This queues until the first round after the switch, at most one heartbeat, and covers the immediate form. Change the step-5 test to effectiveAt >= block.timestamp so the same-block case is caught. Record the change against D-014's no-after-clause default.

findings.title: The reopen freshness test uses updatedAt (transmit time), not startedAt (observation time)
findings.description: Raw entry 15. The B2-2 rule in readStockFeed rejects a round with updatedAt < sessionOpenedAt (line 237) and discards startedAt (line 234). On these OCR2 DualAggregators startedAt is the observation time and updatedAt the transmit time, 12 seconds later on every sampled round (chain-constants section 4). A round observed before the reopen but transmitted after it passes as a round from the new session though it carries the held price.
findings.scenario: At the Sunday 20:00:00 EDT reopen, a round observed at 19:59:55 and transmitted at 20:00:07 shows the Friday price with updatedAt >= sessionOpenedAt. The keeper's settle at the open, which PRD 7.4 says runs at session open and when fresh rounds arrive, buys against it. Observed reopen rounds landed 23 to 48 seconds after 20:00, so the window is narrow and needs the DON to observe while the market is closed. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: Also require startedAt >= sessionOpenedAt, next to the existing updatedAt checks. latestRoundData already returns it, so it costs nothing. Record startedAt on the receipt or derive it in the verifier.

findings.title: The premium cap treats USDG as exactly 1 USD and ignores the USDG/USD answer the guard already read, so the USD premium can pass the cap by up to the depeg tolerance
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 16 (oracle, anchored at SleeveBuy.sol:45, now lines 45-56) and 36 (arithmetic, PriceGuard.sol:299). AUDIT_R1.md lists both under LOW. exceedsPremium (lines 288-301) and premiumBps (line 365) compare USDG spent, in USDG, with tokensOut * answer, where answer is the stock price in USD. checkUsdg accepts USDG/USD anywhere in [0.995, 1.005] and the guard keeps usdgAnswer for the receipt, but the arithmetic never uses it and BuyOrder does not carry it. Any in-band USDG/USD value adds straight onto the owner's cap against the USD reference that PRD 7.4 item 8 and claim C2 describe, and receipts report premiumBps on the par basis. The sell side (exceedsDiscount, discountBps) has the same shape for component 6.
findings.scenario: USDG/USD reads 1.005e8, which passes DEPEG at 50 bps. The rule cap is 100 bps and the SPY feed reads 100 USD. A fill of 101 USDG for 1e18 token units passes exceedsPremium and the receipt shows premiumBps = 100, but in USD the owner paid 101.505 for a 100 USD reference, 150.5 bps. With the feed also trailing the live price by 0.5 percent, a fill at the cap costs about 2.0 percent over the live USD price against PRD 7.4's 'about 1.5 percent' worst case shown in the app (S34), and about 6 percent at the 500 bps maximum. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/arithmetic_Premium.t.sol::ArithmeticPremiumParTest.test_usdgPremiumAddsToCapInUsdTerms.
findings.fix: Convert the reference into USDG before comparing. Carry usdgAnswer in BuyOrder, pass it into exceedsPremium and premiumBps (and exceedsDiscount and discountBps for sells), and compare usdgSpent * usdgAnswer * 10^scale * 10,000 against tokensOut * answer * 10^feedDecimals * (10,000 + cap) with the same 512-bit products, which is the same as using answerUsdg = answer * 10^8 / usdgAnswer. If par is deliberate, add a DECISIONS entry, say on receipts that the premium is in USDG at par, and restate the worst case as cap + 0.5 percent feed lag + 0.5 percent depeg band in the PRD, the app and SECURITY.md.

findings.title: A USDG pause or freeze reverts split and settle wholesale instead of queueing or refusing with a named reason
findings.description: Raw entry 27 (e16bb96 line 438). The guard checks only the stock token side: the registry's isBlocked on the account and pool, token.paused() and oraclePaused() (PriceGuard.checkToken, lines 194-197). It never reads USDG's paused() or isFrozen() for the account, SwapRouter02 or the pool. USDG.approve checks msg.sender and the spender, and transferFrom checks from, to and msg.sender, all under whenNotPaused. So a USDG pause, or a freeze on the account, router or pool, makes the executeFromExecutor batch revert with ContractPaused or AddressFrozen. _buy rethrows it (line 443), the whole split reverts, and not even the spend share is booked or a receipt written. That contrasts with a stock token pause, which queues PAUSED, and with build-contract rule 3 (named custom errors). The issuer freeze is a disclosed risk (PRD 9), so the impact is liveness and observability.
findings.scenario: Paxos freezes SwapRouter02 in USDG, or pauses USDG for a day. Every keeper and public split whose guard would buy reverts AddressFrozen or ContractPaused with no receipt, keepers retry in a loop, and settle reverts the same way. A frozen pool only blocks triggers that pick it, but a frozen router blocks every buy. No PoC was written. A fork test can impersonate USDG's pause or freeze role holder.
findings.fix: In the guard, read usdg.paused() and usdg.isFrozen(x) for the account, router and pool. Queue with PAUSED when USDG is paused or the router or pool is frozen, refuse or revert with a named error when the account is frozen, and treat a failed probe as not frozen. At minimum, catch the batch revert in _buy and rethrow it wrapped in a named error such as BuyReverted(bytes).

groups.name: Lots and sell-back preconditions (SleeveState lots, the unwritten component 6)

findings.title: Lots are never reconciled with the account's stock-token balance, so sell-back can act on phantom lots
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 6 (tokens, MEDIUM) and 18 (funds, LOW), plus the second half of entry 39 (spec), which states the same root cause. Entry 39's main point, lots tied to one module instance, stays separate as A1-28. AUDIT_R1.md lists entries 18 and 39 again under LOW and INFO. createLot (lines 164-172) records tokensBought and tokensRemaining from the measured fill, and nothing afterwards ties a lot to the account's token balance. Owner brackets (SleeveModule._bookOwnerOp, line 409) measure only USDG, so a bracketed batch that moves stock tokens leaves every lot FILLED with full tokensRemaining. PRD 9 and I11 let the owner transfer stock tokens through any ERC-4337 client. onUninstall keeps lots and lotQueues (SPEC 6), so after an uninstall, an outside transfer and a reinstall the old lots are back at the head of the queue. SPEC 12 has sells decrement lots and D-009 Q30 makes tokens outside lots unsellable, but the module cannot tell lot tokens from other tokens by balance. Component 6 is not written, so this is a precondition finding against the shipped lot plumbing. Triage in AUDIT_R1.md: OPEN for component 6.
findings.scenario: The owner gets lot 7 with 10 SPY, then moves the 10 SPY out in a bracketed batch. Lot 7 still shows 10 tokensRemaining, and the app, verifier and receipts show holdings that don't exist. Later 4 SPY arrive from outside Sleeve. sell(SPY, 4, ...) sells those non-lot tokens, contradicting Q30, and writes PART_SOLD receipts against lot 7. Uninstall form: the owner holds a 10-token SPY lot, uninstalls, sends the 10 SPY to an exchange, reinstalls and buys a new 5-token lot. A sell by amount of 5 walks oldest first, picks the empty lot 1, and the swap's transferFrom reverts with an opaque error, so only a sell naming the new lot works. No direct loss, since only the owner can sell. No PoC exists because there is no sell path yet. A verifier can show the stale lot with a bracketed token transfer followed by lot(7).
findings.fix: In component 6, cap each sell at min(sum of the lots' tokensRemaining, token.balanceOf(account)) and measure tokensIn by balance delta as the buy does, skipping or trimming lots whose tokens are gone. Add an owner-callable or automatic lot reconcile that trims tokensRemaining to the balance with a receipt, or extend the bracket to snapshot the balances of tokens with lots and book a negative delta against them, or mark lots stale at uninstall. Document that lots are an upper bound until reconciled, and add a fork test where tokens leave outside Sleeve, including across an uninstall and reinstall, before a sell.

findings.title: The lot transition rule forbids PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD, so a lot can only be partly sold once
findings.description: Raw entry 7. transitionLot (lines 176-185) allows FILLED or SETTLED to PART_SOLD or SOLD, and PART_SOLD to SOLD only. SPEC 12 says each lot a sell touches gets a PART_SOLD or SOLD receipt, and a sell by amount walks lots oldest first, so a second partial sale of a lot already PART_SOLD needs PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD and reverts BadLotTransition. The rule is written into SPEC 14 (docs/SPEC.md line 172) and encoded by test_I7_lotTransitionsOnlyAsAllowed (contracts/test/unit/SleeveModuleInvariants.t.sol:173), so the fix changes I7's table. Component 6 is not written. Triage in AUDIT_R1.md: OPEN for component 6, which will allow PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD, with SPEC 14 and I7 updated.
findings.scenario: An owner sells 3 of a 10-token lot (FILLED to PART_SOLD), then tries to sell 2 more. Sell by amount starts at the head lot, still PART_SOLD with 7 left, and the transition reverts. After the first partial sale the owner can only sell that lot's whole remainder or name a later lot by id. Tokens outside lots aren't sellable through Sleeve in M0 (D-009 Q30), so owners have to over-sell or leave Sleeve to reach their tokens. PoC against e16bb96 (SleeveState unchanged): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/funds_LotTransition.t.sol::test_secondPartialSaleOfALotReverts.
findings.fix: Allow PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD in transitionLot, or have component 6 skip the status write when the status does not change. Either way update SPEC 14 and the I7 allowed-transition list, and change test_I7_lotTransitionsOnlyAsAllowed so the tests encode it.

findings.title: The planned sell-back guard misses the router blocklist that Stock.approve and transferFrom enforce
findings.description: Raw entry 13. checkToken (lines 184-199) tests isBlocked(account) and isBlocked(pool) only. That is enough on a buy, where the pool calls transfer(account). On a sell, Stock.approve checks the spender (SwapRouter02), and the pool callback's transferFrom checks msg.sender (the router), the account and the pool (chain-constants section 3). SPEC 12's mirrored sell guard lists only 'account not blocked', so if component 6 reuses checkToken unchanged, a blocked router turns every sell into an opaque Blocked(address) revert, never a named SellWaits or refusal. Component 6 is not written, so this is a precondition finding.
findings.scenario: The issuer's BLOCKER_ROLE adds SwapRouter02 to the shared registry blocklist. Every sell-back for every ticker reverts inside the account batch with the token's Blocked(router), and the app can't explain why. The owner can still move tokens directly, so no funds are locked. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: For the sell path, check isBlocked(router) next to the account and pool and revert a named error such as RouterBlocked. Add a fork test with the real registry blocking the router, impersonating the BLOCKER_ROLE holder the way the REFUSED_ACCOUNT fork test does.

findings.title: Lot queues grow without bound per account and ticker, and a by-amount sell writes one receipt per lot in a single call
findings.description: Raw entry 19. createLot pushes every FILLED or SETTLED buy onto lotQueues[account][tickerId].ids (line 171), and nothing pops it: SOLD lots stay behind head. SPEC 12 has a by-amount sell walk lots oldest first, write a PART_SOLD or SOLD receipt per touched lot, and revert ExceedsLots unless one call covers the amount. A receipt write alone measured 45,225 gas warm, so with lot updates and the swap, a sell touching a few hundred lots reaches bundler callGasLimits and then the 32M per-transaction limit. lotsOf() returns the whole ids array. Component 6 is not written, so this is a precondition finding.
findings.scenario: A merchant-style account receiving many small payments (the campaign rule at 50 percent with a 1 USDG clip, the keeper splitting each payment) builds up thousands of SPY lots. A 'sell everything' by amount runs out of gas, and lotsOf eth_calls get heavy. An attacker can add lots too, but each one costs at least minClip / equityBps USDG gifted to the victim, so the risk is mostly organic. The owner can still sell lot by lot. Gas PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/dos_UninstallAndLots.t.sol::test_receiptWriteGas.
findings.fix: In component 6, give sell a maxLots bound, or let a by-amount sell fill up to N lots and return the remainder. Keep advancing head over SOLD lots, and emit per-lot fills in one aggregate receipt or event rather than a full receipt each. Add a paged lotsOf(account, ticker, start, count) that starts at head.

findings.title: Lots are keyed to this module instance, so a new module version leaves existing holdings unsellable through sell-back
findings.description: Raw entry 39, first half. Its second half (tokensRemaining never drops when the owner moves tokens out) is merged into A1-03. Lots live in this module's storage, and D-009 Q30 makes tokens outside lots unsellable through Sleeve. PRD 10 requires a new module version whenever the issuer disclosure changes, and PRD 13 says a new version is a new install, so every lot bought under the old version becomes unsellable through sell-back, which is the M0 cash path in PRD 7.5. A spec conflict for component 6, which is not written.
findings.scenario: The issuer edits its disclosure text, and Sleeve ships v2 with the new hash. The owner installs v2. All existing SPY holdings have no v2 lots and can't be sold through Sleeve.
findings.fix: Before writing component 6, decide on lot migration and record it in DECISIONS. Since it touches Q30 and PRD 7.5 it may need the owner. Options: a v2 import of v1 lots verified against v1 receipt hashes, or a sell path for unlotted balances under the same guard. Cap any sell at min(lot remaining, the account's token balance).

findings.title: Sell-back must record its proceeds in the bracket's module delta, or endOwnerOp books them to spend a second time
findings.description: Raw entry 46. Guidance for component 6, not a bug in the snapshot. endOwnerOp books ownerDelta = balanceNow - balanceAtBegin - moduleDelta (SleeveModule._bookOwnerOp, line 412), and today only _recordFill (SleeveTrade.sol line 466) calls recordModuleDelta (SleeveState.sol line 108). A sell the owner runs inside its bracket (SPEC: 'normally inside an owner bracket') that credits proceeds to spend directly, without recordModuleDelta(+usdgOut), would have endOwnerOp book the same proceeds again as an owner inflow.
findings.scenario: The owner sells a lot for 100 USDG inside [beginOwnerOp, sell, endOwnerOp]. The sell credits spend +100, endOwnerOp sees ownerDelta = +100 and credits spend +100 again, so spend sits 100 above the real balance. The next split reconciles, but until then the ledger shows 100 USDG of spend that doesn't exist, which the next owner outflow can pull from buckets.
findings.fix: In the sell path, call SleeveState.recordModuleDelta(account, int256(usdgOut)) after measuring proceeds by balance delta, mirroring _recordFill. Add a fork test with a bracketed sell that checks spend equals balance minus pending after endOwnerOp.

findings.title: Lot plumbing has no ownership check, so component 6 must enforce lot.account and the ticker
findings.description: Raw entry 47. transitionLot (lines 176-185) checks only that the lot exists and that the transition is allowed. It does not check the caller, the account, the ticker or tokensRemaining. Lot ids are global (they are receipt ids), lots and lotQueues outlive uninstall, and fake accounts (A1-23) create lots in the same id space. Nothing is exposed today. It is a precondition for component 6.
findings.scenario: If component 6 adds a sell-by-lot entry point that takes a lotId and trusts it, one account could transition another account's lot and corrupt its attribution, or a lot could be sold under the wrong ticker's pool and guard.
findings.fix: In component 6, require lot.account == the account being sold for (and msg.sender == account for owner-only sells and the off-hours override) and lot.tickerId == tickerId. Decrement tokensRemaining and measure tokens leaving by balance delta, because the owner can move tokens out outside Sleeve (I11, A1-03).

groups.name: Install, uninstall, keeper and self-registered accounts (SleeveModule, account trust)

findings.title: onUninstall's bucket release needs about 250k to 330k gas, and a callGasLimit inside the silent band removes the module but skips the release
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 12 (dos, LOW) and 45 (aa, INFO). AUDIT_R1.md lists entry 45 again under INFO. onUninstall (lines 155-162) releases every non-empty bucket and writes a RELEASED receipt for each: a hash SSTORE, a full-receipt event, and TokenSource and calendar reads. Kernel v3.1 calls onUninstall through ExcessivelySafeCall with gasleft() and ignores the result (g6-notes section 7, D-019). If the UserOp's callGasLimit leaves Kernel its last 1/64 but not enough for the release, Kernel removes the module and emits ModuleUninstallResult(false), while SleeveModule keeps installed = true, pendingTotal and the buckets, with no RELEASED receipts and no Uninstalled event. Measured: 250,271 gas on the unit harness with four warm buckets. On the fork at block 78,312,136 under --isolate, callGasLimit 250k and 300k remove the module silently and 330k completes the release. Without --isolate the band is about 120k to 300k, and 150k reverts the whole op. The app floor of 400k leaves about 70k of headroom on forge's EVM, which does not model ArbOS or L1 pricing. A bundler's eth_estimateUserOperationGas binary-searches for the lowest callGasLimit that does not revert, and lands inside the band because the outer call succeeds either way. No funds move: USDG stays in the account and onInstall cleans the stale state on reinstall.
findings.scenario: An owner uninstalls through a sponsored UserOp whose callGasLimit came from the bundler's estimate, about 200k, while four buckets are pending. The op succeeds, Kernel no longer lists the module, ModuleUninstallResult is false, isInitialized stays true and pendingTotal stays put, so the app and verifier show buckets that were never released and no Uninstalled event exists. PoCs against e16bb96 (SleeveModule unchanged): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/dos_UninstallAndLots.t.sol (test_onUninstallGasWithFourBuckets, and test_shortGasUninstallLeavesStaleState, where MockAccount.uninstallModule{gas: 120_000} completes with pendingTotal still 120e6) and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/aa_UninstallGas.t.sol::test_sweepUninstallCallGas (fork sweep).
findings.fix: App: release the buckets in the same bracketed batch before uninstallModule so onUninstall is cheap, never accept a bundler estimate for the uninstall (keep the 400k floor, or set callGasLimit from the previewed bucket count times about 90k plus margin), and assert ModuleUninstallResult(module, true). Contract, as defense in depth: a permissionless prune(account) that runs only when the account no longer lists the module and acct.installed is true, releases the buckets with RELEASED receipts and deletes the state, so anyone, the keeper included, can close out a skipped release. Document the band in docs/GAS.md next to the measured release.

findings.title: The module-wide transient reentrancy lock lets any self-installed contract make other accounts' Sleeve calls fail while it holds control
findings.description: Raw entry 29. ReentrancyGuardTransient uses one lock slot for the whole module, not one per account. split and settle hold it while SleeveBuy calls account.executeFromExecutor (SleeveBuy.sol line 71), which hands control to the account. Any contract can install the module on itself (D-015) and, as OWNER, call split on its own ledger to get control inside executeFromExecutor with the lock held. Every Sleeve entry point reached from there reverts ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall for every account, including beginOwnerOp, which the app puts first in every owner UserOp (I14). The attacker then runs the module's own batch so the buy postconditions pass and the outer split succeeds, and nothing it did is rolled back. EntryPoint v0.7 has no EOA-only check on handleOps callers, unlike v0.8. No ledger corruption.
findings.scenario: A malicious bundler wraps EntryPoint.handleOps inside its fake account's executeFromExecutor during its own split, which needs at least a 1 USDG clip and an open market. Each honest owner UserOp in that bundle passes validation and then reverts at beginOwnerOp in execution. handleOps does not revert, so the victims pay actualGasCost to the bundler and their actions are delayed. PoC against e16bb96 (SleeveModule unchanged): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/transient_Audit.t.sol::test_globalLockFailsOtherAccountsOwnerOpNestedInAnotherBuy, where a victim owner op nested inside another account's split fails with ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall and its transfer does not happen.
findings.fix: Key the lock per account. Owner entry points (onInstall, onUninstall, setRule, pauseRule, resumeRule, setKeeper, beginOwnerOp, endOwnerOp, release) lock on msg.sender, and split, settle and observe lock on the target account, using a transient slot derived like SleeveState.beginSlot. That keeps same-account reentrancy blocked without one account's buy blocking every other account. Before adopting it, check that cross-account reentry during a buy cannot disturb shared state, such as the receipt counter _recordFill reads after the buy to pick the lot id (SleeveTrade.sol line 474). If the global lock stays, record the bundler griefing vector in DECISIONS and SECURITY.md.

findings.title: defaultKeeper is immutable and shared by every account, so a leaked KEEPER key cannot be rotated centrally
findings.description: Raw entry 30. An install without a keeper writes the immutable defaultKeeper into acct.keeper (line 141). KEEPER is one EOA (D-004) and becomes the keeper of every account the app installs. The PRD 14 row 'Trigger timed for the worst price inside the cap' holds because the keeper or the owner triggers first and the public waits out the grace. A stolen keeper key keeps the no-grace trigger, with a caller-chosen pool and quote (minOut near zero, D-009 Q21, A1-06), on every account. The only remedy is each owner signing setKeeper, and new installs keep getting the leaked default for the life of the immutable module. The power equals a public caller's after the grace, so it fits the PRD's wording, but nothing revokes it centrally.
findings.scenario: KEEPER leaks. The attacker pushes an allowlisted pool up to just under each account's premium cap against the feed, calls split or settle as KEEPER for every account with unsorted or pending USDG, then sells back. It takes up to premiumCapBps (up to 500 bps) of every equity buy across all default-keeper accounts until each owner rotates. Without the key, a public caller could only do this after the grace, by which time the honest keeper has already sorted. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: Treat acct.keeper == address(0) as 'use the module's current default', read from a pointer that SleeveTimelock can rotate or the deployer can only clear, and use a sentinel such as address(1) for 'no keeper'. Otherwise document a forced setKeeper migration in the app and keeper runbook and have the app pass an explicit keeper at install. A1-06's on-chain minOut floor would also cap what a stolen key can take.

findings.title: Any contract can self-register, get the default keeper, and write genuine-looking FILLED receipts and lots with fabricated fills into the shared log
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 31 (aa, anchored at SleeveModule.sol:141) and 37 (access, SleeveBuy.sol:68, now line 71). AUDIT_R1.md lists both under LOW. onInstall accepts any msg.sender, and a zero keeper in the data assigns defaultKeeper. _enter (SleeveTrade.sol lines 484-501) only checks that the account answers isModuleInstalled(2, module) == 1 (_listsModule, line 505), which any contract can do. SleeveBuy then calls account.executeFromExecutor (line 71) and trusts the account's own balance deltas (lines 68-78), so a fake account can spend exactly amountIn USDG to any address and mint or pull stock tokens from elsewhere with no swap. The module writes a FILLED receipt with venue Uniswap v3, an allowlisted pool, the real feed round, a premium the account chose, a stored hash that recomputes cleanly, and a lot. D-015 says a fake account reaches only its own state, which holds for ledgers but not for the shared receipt log, the lot id space or the shared default keeper. Second effect, from entry 31: every fake account also gets Sleeve's default keeper, so a keeper that triggers every Installed account with keeper == defaultKeeper sends real transactions into attacker code that can burn the gas limit. No user funds are at risk.
findings.scenario: An attacker deploys FakeFillAccount, calls onInstall with keeper 0 and the default rule, sends itself 500 USDG, then calls split(self, allowlistedPool, quote) as OWNER. Its executeFromExecutor sends 50 USDG to a sink and mints tokens. Receipt N is FILLED with tokensOut 1e30 and premiumBps below -9,000, lot N exists, receiptHash(N) matches the event, and the router never received USDG. Repeating this fills the public receipt log and skews any README, HP1 or verifier number that aggregates receipts module-wide, and registering many accounts makes the keeper pay gas on them. PoCs against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/aa_FakeAccountReceipts.t.sol::test_selfRegisteredContractWritesFabricatedFillReceipt and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/access_Observe.t.sol::test_access_fakeAccountMintsAFilledReceiptAtAnyPrice. The snapshot's test/mocks/TamperingAccount.sol is a ready base.
findings.fix: Contract: tie the fill to the pool by reading the pool's USDG and token balances before and after the batch and requiring that the pool received exactly amountIn USDG and released exactly tokensOut, and stop giving self-registered callers the default keeper (require an explicit keeper in the install data, or let the keeper opt in off chain). Verifier, keeper and metrics, written into SPEC as a requirement: count a receipt only when the account's code is the Kernel v3.1 ERC-1967 proxy (61-byte runtime, implementation slot 0xBAC8...4b4D as reported) and the FILLED or SETTLED transaction has a matching pool Swap event with recipient == account and the same amounts. The keeper applies the same codehash filter and a hard gas cap before it triggers any account.

findings.title: onUninstall wipes the account's state even when Kernel still lists the executor (uninstallModule with type 4, 5 or 6, or a direct call)
findings.description: Raw entry 32. Kernel v3.1 uninstallModule for types 4, 5 and 6 force-calls module.onUninstall through ModuleLib without checking that the module is installed as that type (lib/kernel/src/Kernel.sol lines 457-496), and the account can also call onUninstall directly from a batch. Types 5 and 6 slice deInitData[0:32] first, so they need at least 32 bytes of data, while type 4 with empty data reaches onUninstall. SleeveModule.onUninstall (lines 155-162) releases the buckets and deletes the account's state without checking that the account stopped listing it as an executor. That is the reverse of the drift D-019 handles: Kernel lists the executor while isInitialized is false, so every split and settle reverts NotInstalled, and arriving USDG is never sorted until a reinstall moves it all to spend through the install snapshot. Only an owner-signed action can cause it.
findings.scenario: The owner's client, an SDK helper or a dapp-built batch the owner signs sends uninstallModule(4, sleeveModule, "") by mistake, for example while removing an executor hook. Kernel calls Sleeve.onUninstall, which releases the buckets and deletes the ledgers while executorConfig(sleeve).hook stays address(1). Paychecks then sit unsorted, and when the app reinstalls, the snapshot moves them all to spend, so the equity share of that income is never invested. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: In onUninstall, check that the account no longer lists the module (the _listsModule test from SleeveTrade, line 505) and revert if it still does. Kernel's executor path clears executorConfig before calling onUninstall, so a real uninstall passes, and Kernel swallows the revert on the wrong-type paths, so state is kept. Optionally onInstall can require the listing too, since Kernel writes executorConfig before onInstall, which rejects installs as a fallback or hook type. Confirm both orderings in lib/kernel and against the G6 notes, and check the interplay with A1-07's silent skip.

groups.name: Split outcomes, reconcile and receipt fields (SleeveTrade._sort, _reconcile, _queue)

findings.title: A split whose equity part is zero writes QUEUED with reason CLIP although nothing is queued
findings.description: Merged from raw entries 20 (spec, LOW, e16bb96 line 241) and 48 (arithmetic, INFO, line 242). AUDIT_R1.md lists entry 48 again under INFO. When floor(unsorted * equityBps / 10,000) == 0, _sort (lines 246-247) writes status QUEUED, reason CLIP and usdgQueued 0, leaves the bucket alone, and sends the whole amount to spend. That covers every split under a 0 bps equity rule (setRule accepts equityBps 0, because validateShares(10000, 0) passes) and dust payments under small shares. I2 holds, but PRD 7.6 and SPEC 9 step 7 define QUEUED as equity entering pending, so the receipt says money waits when all of it went to spend. previewSplit (lines 188-190) reports the same, and the repo's own test_split_zeroEquityPart_sortsEverythingToSpendWithoutTheGuard (contracts/test/unit/SleeveModuleSplit.t.sol:550) encodes it.
findings.scenario: The owner sets a 100 percent spend rule (spendBps 10,000, equityBps 0) and a 500 USDG payment arrives. The keeper's split writes QUEUED/CLIP with usdgToSpend 500e6 and usdgQueued 0. The inbox, history, five-day queue prompt and verifier show a queued item that no settle can ever clear. PoC against e16bb96: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-sleeve/e8745a41-dfe5-4389-9aa3-ac2131949975/scratchpad/audit-r1/contracts/test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol::test_zeroEquityRuleWritesQueuedClipWithNothingQueued.
findings.fix: Reject equityBps == 0 in _validateRule, since an ACTIVE rule implies an equity share, and give a split whose equity part rounds to zero a distinct outcome: a status meaning all of it went to spend, or reason NONE with usdgQueued 0. Or keep QUEUED/CLIP and have the app and verifier key on usdgQueued == 0. Document the choice in SPEC 13 and update the repo test that encodes today's behavior.

findings.title: RECONCILED receipts repurpose usdgSpent and usdgQueued
findings.description: Raw entry 22 (e16bb96 line 335). _reconcile (lines 321-345) sets usdgIn = fromSpend + fromPending, usdgSpent = fromSpend (USDG taken off the spend ledger) and usdgQueued = fromPending (USDG taken off buckets). Everywhere else usdgSpent means equity USDG paid to the venue and usdgQueued means USDG added to pending. SPEC 13 and D-019 only say 'totals'. A consumer that sums usdgSpent as invested capital, or checks I2 per receipt, reads a third-party pull as a buy. PRD 7.10 and the README numbers rule depend on these fields.
findings.scenario: An old approval pulls 50 USDG. The next split writes RECONCILED with usdgSpent 50 and usdgQueued 0. The app's 'equity bought' total and the verifier's per-status math pick up 50 USDG of phantom investment unless every consumer special-cases RECONCILED. The verifier can check how packages/core and the app's receipt code sum these fields. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: Document the RECONCILED field mapping in SPEC 13, or add explicit fields (or reuse the usdgOut and tokensIn meanings) so usdgSpent keeps one meaning. Add a verifier test vector for RECONCILED.

findings.title: Income arriving before an outside pull is reconciled is netted against the shortfall and isn't split in full
findings.description: Raw entry 40 (e16bb96 line 95). split reconciles only when unsorted is 0 (lines 102-106). If USDG leaves through an old approval (a shortfall) and a payment lands before any split reconciles, unsorted = balance - spend - pending (line 100) already absorbs the shortfall, and part of the payment silently refills the spend ledger instead of being split. It's inherent to balance-based accounting and matches the PRD formula, so the open question is whether it is documented.
findings.scenario: spend 100, an outside pull of 100, then a 1,000 USDG payment before the keeper runs. The split sorts 900 and invests 10 percent of 900, not 1,000. Some of the payment that should have been invested goes to spend.
findings.fix: Have the keeper call split as soon as previewSplit shows a shortfall above zero, since that split reconciles. Document the netting in DECISIONS and the receipt explainer.

findings.title: bucket.reason is the latest queue reason and settle never updates it, so the five-day same-reason prompt can't be driven from chain state
findings.description: Raw entry 43 (e16bb96 line 355). _queue overwrites bucket.reason with each new part's reason (line 360) while since stays at the first queue time, and settle reverts GuardNotClear with no state change (line 286). So the reason a bucket is actually waiting on, such as PREMIUM after a weekend SESSION queue, is never recorded. PRD 7.4 and the PRD 14 row 'Token trades at a sustained premium' ask for an owner prompt after five days queued for the same reason.
findings.scenario: A bucket is queued SESSION on Saturday. From Monday every settle simulation fails PREMIUM. bucketOf still shows SESSION with since on Saturday, so the app or keeper has to rebuild the reason history from receipts and simulations, and bucket state alone gives a wrong prompt.
findings.fix: State in SPEC that the prompt comes from keeper simulations and receipts, or store a per-reason since that a settle attempt can refresh.

groups.name: Admin powers, pool allowlist and calendar coverage (TokenSource, SleeveTimelock, SessionCalendarExtension, SleeveTrade._guard step 1)

findings.title: A trigger's pool off a non-empty allowlist reverts PoolNotAllowed where SPEC 9 and PRD 7.4 say REFUSED_TICKER, and no DECISIONS entry records it
findings.description: Raw entry 23 (e16bb96 line 382). PRD 7.4 step 1 includes 'the pool is on the ticker's allowlist', and failing step 1 makes the leg REFUSED_TICKER with its USDG sent to spend. SPEC 9 step 5.1 says the same. _guard returns REFUSED_TICKER only when the allowlist is empty (line 388) and reverts PoolNotAllowed for a pool off a non-empty list (line 392), for split and settle. The behavior is safer, since a public caller cannot push equity into spend by passing a bad pool, but it contradicts the PRD and SPEC and is recorded only in the code comment (lines 369-373). The build contract says a PRD conflict is reported to the owner, not chosen. test_fork_poolNotAllowed_reverts (contracts/test/fork/SleeveModuleSplit.t.sol:202) encodes the deviation as acceptance behavior.
findings.scenario: The keeper passes a pool that the timelock removed after the keeper cached the list. The PRD expects a REFUSED_TICKER receipt with the equity in spend. The code reverts and writes no receipt, so the keeper, verifier and claim ledger built from SPEC 9 wait for a receipt that never comes.
findings.fix: Keep the revert, and since the PRD wins, raise it with the owner. Then add a DECISIONS entry and update SPEC 9 step 5.1 and SPEC 10 so step 1 reads: ticker inactive, no feed or empty allowlist gives REFUSED_TICKER, and a trigger pool off a non-empty allowlist reverts PoolNotAllowed.

findings.title: An empty pool allowlist on an active ticker turns every split's equity part and every settled bucket into spend
findings.description: Raw entry 24 (e16bb96 line 383). When poolsOf(tickerId) is empty, _guard returns REFUSE_TICKER (lines 388-391) though the ticker is still active. Split sends each new equity part to spend, and settle, which the keeper or anyone after the grace can call, sends whole buckets to spend as REFUSED_TICKER. TokenSource.setPool(id, pool, false) can empty the list (_disallowPool, TokenSource.sol line 276). Swapping a pool takes two separate 48-hour operations, so if the removal executes first there is a window where queued equity across all accounts can be pushed to spend by anyone. D-009 Q24 and PRD 9 tie that outcome to removing the ticker, not to rotating pools, and PRD 14 says the admin can only remove tickers and cannot change rules. Per raw entry 44, REFUSED_TICKER for an empty allowlist is covered only by a unit test.
findings.scenario: The timelock executes setPool(SPY, oldPool, false) before setPool(SPY, newPool, true). During the gap, keeper splits for SPY rules write REFUSED_TICKER, and a public caller settles every SPY bucket past its grace into spend. No funds leave the account, but the equity share for affected payments is lost to spend for good. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: Treat an empty allowlist on an active ticker as a QUEUE reason (or revert NoPool), and keep REFUSED_TICKER for removal and a missing feed. Or make TokenSource refuse a removal that would leave an active ticker with no pools. At minimum, document add-before-remove in the timelock runbook and the proposal script.

findings.title: The 48-hour admin delay is never bound on chain, because TokenSource, the calendar extension and the module accept any contract as timelock
findings.description: Raw entry 34. TokenSource (line 168) and SessionCalendarExtension (line 131) check only timelock_.code.length != 0. The SleeveModule constructor (lines 94-115) checks USDG, decimals and the router's factory, but not that tokenSource.timelock() == calendar.timelock() or that the timelock enforces MIN_DELAY_FLOOR. Chain 4663 supports EIP-7702 (the report cites ArbOS 61), so a delegated EOA has code and passes. SleeveTimelock's constructor (line 48) also accepts address(0) among executors, which its own NatSpec (lines 44-45) warns about. The documented admin bound (D-004, D-018, PRD 14: 'behind a timelock, with a public event') rests on deploy-script discipline, and nothing on chain enforces it.
findings.scenario: The deploy script passes DEPLOYER (7702-delegated), a plain TimelockController with a 0 delay, or two different timelocks. Every check passes. removeTicker, setPool, appendYear and replaceFutureSwitch then run with no 48-hour public window, and the immutable module is bound to them for good, so the admin could open a closed calendar instant or swap pools at once. No PoC was written. A unit test that deploys TokenSource and the module against a zero-delay TimelockController shows it.
findings.fix: In the SleeveModule constructor, require tokenSource.timelock() == calendar.timelock(), SleeveTimelock(t).MIN_DELAY_FLOOR() == 172_800 and t.getMinDelay() >= that floor, and optionally pin the timelock's extcodehash. In the SleeveTimelock constructor, revert when an executor or proposer is address(0) or either list is empty. Have the deploy script read these back from chain as postconditions.

findings.title: A ticker's session type is fixed at construction, so a ticker that loses overnight trading cannot be moved to REGULAR
findings.description: Raw entry 35. sessionType is written once, in _list (lines 247-265), from the constructor. TokenSource exposes only removeTicker and setPool, and nothing lists a ticker again (I10). So the REGULAR branch of SessionCalendar.decide and _openedAt, which research names as the safe mapping (session-calendar.md Q2) for a ticker that loses overnight tradability, can't be reached in production. PRD 7.4 takes the per-ticker session type from the issuer's tradability field, which can change. The calendar's in-range writes (addClosure, addEarlyClose) only act on whole days or the 13:00 or 17:00 early close, so they can't express 'closed 20:00 to 09:30'. The only lever is removeTicker after 48 hours, which is permanent. Related: A1-02 is the same held-price symptom for unscheduled day closures.
findings.scenario: The overnight venue stops for weeks, as Blue Ocean ATS did after 5 Aug 2024, or the issuer flips tradingCapabilities.overnight for NVDA. The 24/5 feed holds the 20:00 round overnight. SleeveTrade._guard (line 382) still gets open = true with openedAt at the Sunday 20:00 reopen, and the held round passes the 25-hour age check and updatedAt >= openedAt. After-hours news drops the real price 8 percent. An attacker holding tokens lifts the thin overnight pool to just under the held answer times (1 + premiumCap) and fires a public settle on a queued bucket once its grace has run. The module buys about 8 percent plus the cap above the real market, every night until the timelock acts, and removing the ticker sends every later equity share to spend. No PoC was written.
findings.fix: Add a timelocked TokenSource.tightenSessionType(id, newType) that allows only ALL_DAY to REGULAR, or anything to NONE, emits an event and bumps a version the receipts record. Like addClosure, refuse it once it would change an answer for an instant already past. Or give SessionCalendarExtension a per-type overnight-closure range. Record the decision in DECISIONS either way.

findings.title: Expired calendar coverage reads as an ordinary SESSION queue, so the OUT_OF_RANGE reason is dropped and nothing warns before the 2028 cliff
findings.description: Raw entry 49 (e16bb96 line 377). _guard reads calendar.sessionState (line 382) and drops the calendar's Reason, so an expired calendar (OUT_OF_RANGE) and a normal weekend give the same QUEUED/SESSION receipt, preview and GuardNotClear(SESSION). SPEC 9 step 4 merges them on purpose, but the build contract's 'no silent fallback' rule and research Q8 expected coverage expiry to be visible. The extension starts with endDay = 1 Jan 2028 (SessionCalendarExtension.sol line 134). Dec 31 2027 is a Friday and Jan 1 2028 a Saturday, so the first instant that changes is Sun 2 Jan 2028 20:00 EST (1830474000), the open for Mon 3 Jan, and appendYear(2028) has to be scheduled on the 48-hour timelock before about 31 Dec 2027 20:00 EST. Liveness only: funds wait in buckets until the year is appended.
findings.scenario: No one schedules appendYear(2028) in time. From 1830474000 every split queues and every settle reverts GuardNotClear(SESSION) on a normal Monday. The receipts look like a weekend's, so the keeper and verifier can't tell an expired calendar from a closed market unless they also call coverageEnd().
findings.fix: Carry the calendar Reason into Guard and either add a COVERAGE reason (appended, since the types say the numbering never changes) or put the calendar reason in previews. Have the keeper alert when coverageEnd() - now < 30 days, and add a deploy-checklist item to schedule appendYear(2028) by early December 2027.

result.summary:
I reviewed docs/GATES.md (all sections except G6), docs/research/gates-checks.md, CONTRIBUTIONS.md and docs/CLAIM_LEDGER.md against the research files and with fresh read-only calls, then fixed what was wrong. GATES and gates-checks were accurate: every number and quote I rechecked matched, so I only made three precision fixes and added a recheck record. CONTRIBUTIONS was accurate except four issues. The claim ledger had gone stale since e27701b, and its row 8.1 contradicted GATES G1.

What I checked:
- **Numbers:** 47 groups of numbers, 46 matched. Against the chain: G1 markets, the Morpho deploy block and its deploy receipt, the oracle replays, G2 fees and router code size, G3 asset API hash and ids, G4 rounds and ages, G5 premiums and pool reads, the G7 permit, the G8 verifier, and the C1, C2, Z1, Z2, Z5, M1 and O1 values. Locally: the HP2 figures, the disclosure keccak and every cited test name.
- **Quotes:** about 62, all word for word against the live Robinhood docs bundle, Chainlink sources on GitHub, ERC-8056, EIP-7951, ERC-7562, the ZeroDev docs and Relay.
- **MEASURED rows:** all 19 have rerunnable evidence at HEAD. The unit suite at HEAD passes 508 of 508, and all three --check scripts and hp2 verify.py exit 0.

Fixes in CONTRIBUTIONS.md:
- PriceGuard was listed as "Published". The repo has no remote and isn't public, so I reworded it to match ledger row 5.10, which is PENDING.
- The HP2 paragraph said the replay runs "the same checks", but the protocol leaves out the blocklist.
- It said "the other 934 payments", but 31 plus 934 is not 1,000. I added the qualifier "whose arrival fill was within the 100 bps cap" and the D-020 wording.
- The Z3 quote contained a double hyphen. I split it at that point, following the file's own long-dash rule.

Fixes in GATES.md:
- The intro now says PRD section 22 only defines RESOLVED.
- The G1 paraphrase of the PRD now says the PRD found no source showing such a market, not that none existed.
- The G5 depth-walk pointer now names Appendices A and C.

Fixes in CLAIM_LEDGER.md (statuses unchanged, still on e27701b per rule 4):
- 8.1 and 8.2 now match GATES G1 and G2. Row 8.1 had said no Morpho market lends USDG against a launch ticker.
- 5.9 said CONTRIBUTIONS.md didn't exist. 5.10 now records the LICENSE file and that the repo isn't public.
- 6.5 cited a test that was renamed in a2f58bf. 4.2 now has the new constructor grace check.
- 3.3 claimed the README states the WRAPPED limit. It doesn't.
- 9.22 and 5.7 said no audit exists. They now describe audit round 1 as an internal review.

Component 6 is built, and both round 1 audit findings for sell-back are fixed. The full non-spike suite passes: 710 tests, 0 failures. That is the 620 from before plus 90 new ones (62 unit, 22 fork, 5 gas, 1 lot-transition test).

What the sell does:
- `sell(tickerId, tokenAmount, lotId, pool, quote, overrideClosed, overrideCapBps)` runs in a new delegatecalled library, SleeveSell. Only the account can call it. It works with a paused or missing rule.
- `lotId` 0 sells oldest lot first from the queue head and skips empty lots. Any other `lotId` sells only that lot, which must belong to the caller and the ticker.
- A sell is capped by both the lots (`ExceedsLots`) and the account's token balance (`ExceedsBalance`). This is the phantom-lots fix.
- The swap is one batch on the account: token approve to the router, `exactInputSingle` with the account as recipient, approve back to 0. Afterwards it checks by balance change that exactly the amount left, at least minOut arrived, the allowance is 0 and the module's own balances did not change.
- Proceeds go to spend and into the open bracket's module delta, so they are never split.
- Each lot touched gets one PART_SOLD or SOLD receipt with its pro rata share; the last lot takes the rounding remainder. Price and discount on each receipt are the whole sell's.

Guard order:
1. Lots, ticker feed, pool allowlisted (a removed ticker still sells), balance.
2. Account, pool and router not blocked. I added the router check (`RouterBlocked`) because the token's approve and transferFrom check the router; this was a round 1 LOW.
3. Paused, oracle paused, multiplier due, USDG out of band. These revert `GuardNotClear` with or without the override.
4. Session closed, then a stale feed (age or round from before the reopen). These revert `SellWaits` unless `overrideClosed` is set.

Under the override, a feed answer that is not positive or comes from the future reverts `GuardNotClear(STALE)`. The steps the override can't skip run first, so the app never offers an override that can't help.

Lot transition fix: PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD is now allowed, and the I7 tests are updated. New `reconcileLots(tickerId)` trims lots newest first down to the token balance.
